Payment Posting & Reconciliation

Where Every Payment Gets Checked Against What It Should Be

Payment posting is the step where a payer's remittance, whether an electronic ERA or a paper EOB, gets applied line by line to the correct claim, with contractual adjustments, deductibles, coinsurance and patient responsibility all calculated accurately. Done carelessly, posting errors quietly distort every downstream report: A/R looks wrong, denial rates look wrong, and revenue trends become impossible to trust.

Posting is also where underpayments hide. A payment that looks fine at a glance can still fall short of the contracted rate for that payer and procedure, and unless every payment is checked line by line against the fee schedule, that shortfall never gets flagged or recovered.

PMEX posts every payment the same day the remittance arrives, reconciles it against deposits and the contracted allowable, and flags anything that does not match for immediate follow-up.

How a Payment Moves

From Remittance to Reconciled Balance

Step 1

Remittance Received

ERA or EOB arrives from the payer and is matched to the original claim.

Step 2

Line-by-Line Posting

Payments, adjustments and denials posted against each claim line.

Step 3

Underpayment Check

Payment checked against the contracted rate and flagged if short.

Step 4

Reconciliation

Posted amounts matched against bank deposits to close the loop.

Patient Responsibility

Accurate Balances, Sent Once, Not Corrected Twice

Once insurance adjudicates a claim, whatever is left, deductible, coinsurance or a non-covered service, becomes the patient's responsibility. If that balance is calculated wrong, the statement has to be corrected and resent, which delays payment and frustrates patients.

PMEX calculates patient responsibility only after the insurance payment is fully posted and verified, so the first statement a patient receives is the right one.

Contractual Adjustments

Applied automatically based on the payer's negotiated rate.

Secondary Transfers

Balances routed automatically to secondary or tertiary payers.

Clean Statements

Patient balances shown clearly, with what insurance covered explained.

Payment Posting: Frequently Asked Questions

An ERA is the electronic remittance advice payers send for automated posting. An EOB is the paper or PDF explanation of benefits used when electronic remittance is not available and posting is done manually.

Remittances are posted the same day they are received, so A/R and revenue reporting stay current instead of lagging behind actual payments.

Every posted amount is checked automatically against the contracted fee schedule for that payer and procedure, and anything short of that amount is flagged for A/R follow-up.

Only after the insurance payment and contractual adjustment are fully posted, so the deductible, coinsurance or non-covered balance shown to the patient is accurate the first time.

Yes. Every posted payment is reconciled against actual bank deposits each cycle, so the numbers in your dashboard always match the money that actually arrived.
